subject: Climate & Environment
title: Gas Stoves and NO₂
description: Learn Gas Stoves and NO₂ in one minute.

hook.text: A gas stove running for an hour can push indoor NO₂ above outdoor air quality limits.

buildup.text: Natural gas combustion releases NO₂, CO, and formaldehyde directly into your kitchen.

discovery.text: A Stanford study linked gas stoves to 12.7% of childhood asthma cases in the US.

twist.text: Many homes have no range hood. Those that do often vent air right back into the kitchen.

climax.text: Induction stoves eliminate combustion entirely — no gas, no flame, no indoor pollution.

punchline.text: The flame under the pan may be the biggest polluter in your home.

quiz.question: What percentage of US childhood asthma cases are linked to gas stoves?

details.summary: Gas stoves release nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, and formaldehyde directly into kitchens, often exceeding outdoor air quality standards within minutes. Research links gas stove use to a 42 percent increase in childhood asthma symptoms.
details.whyItMatters: Hundreds of millions of households cook with gas. Evidence connecting indoor NO2 to childhood asthma is reshaping building codes and appliance standards worldwide.
takeaways: Gas burners emit NO2, CO, and formaldehyde into living spaces
Indoor NO2 can exceed outdoor standards within minutes of cooking
Range hoods vented outdoors significantly reduce indoor pollution

faq.question: Do gas stoves really increase childhood asthma risk?
faq.answer: A 2022 meta-analysis found that children in homes with gas stoves had a 42 percent higher risk of current asthma symptoms. The mechanism involves chronic exposure to NO2 inflaming developing airways.

faq.question: Can a range hood solve the problem?
faq.answer: A range hood vented to the outside removes 50 to 80 percent of cooking pollutants when used properly. However, many hoods recirculate air through filters that do not capture gases like NO2, and many people do not use them consistently.
